AnchorX.description: Where along the panel width an actor would like to stand.
AnchorX.title: AnchorX

BalloonKind.description: What kind of balloon carries a line, which is how it gets drawn.
BalloonKind.title: BalloonKind

CameraAngle.description: The camera's height relative to the subject.
CameraAngle.title: CameraAngle

angle.description: The camera's height: `low` looks up, leaving little air above the head; `high` looks down, leaving more.

shot.description: How tightly the camera frames the cast, named by where the frame cuts the body, from `long_shot` to `extreme_close_up`. The tightest it may go: the camera steps back when the cast does not fit.

CaptionEvent.description: One caption box: the panel speaking in its own voice.

by.description: Who is speaking, for a `spoken` caption only: any name, in the cast or not.
by.title: By

kind.description: What the box is doing: `locale` for a place and time, `monologue` for an inner voice, `spoken` for speech from off panel, `editorial` for the writer's voice.

prefer.description: Where the box would like to sit, one of nine zones of the panel. Left out, where reading starts: `top_left`, or `top_right` read right to left.

text.description: What the box says, as one string; line breaks are computed. A word between underscores, `_word_`, is stressed.
text.title: Text

tone.description: What the box is filled with: `paper`, `pale`, `ink`, which is lettered in paper, or `warm`, yellow under `palette: tinted`.

CaptionEvent.title: CaptionEvent

CaptionKind.description: What a caption box is doing, which is how it gets set.
CaptionKind.title: CaptionKind

CaptionTone.description: The value a caption box is filled with.
CaptionTone.title: CaptionTone

CastMember.description: One character present in the panel: a puppet Scenet poses, or a figure a picture draws.

at.description: Where along the panel's width the figure would like to stand. A preference: non-overlap and `left_of` override it.

expression.description: An expression the puppet declares, by name.
expression.title: Expression

facing.description: Which way the figure is turned, `left` or `right`, gaze and all.

figure.description: A figure the panel's picture draws, by the name its artwork contract gives it. Written instead of `reference`, and with none of the keys that pose or place a puppet.
figure.title: Figure

marks.description: Emanata drawn around the character -- `plewds`, `squeans`, `grawlixes`, `briffits` -- in any order, each once. They compose with the expression.
marks.title: Marks

pose.description: A pose the puppet declares, by name.
pose.title: Pose

reference.description: The puppet to draw: a shipped puppet's name, or the path of a `.puppet.yaml` file, relative to the document. Written instead of `figure`.
reference.title: Reference

CastMember.title: CastMember

Column.description: Panels stacked top to bottom, beside the other columns of a tier.

panels.description: The panels in the column, read top to bottom.
panels.title: Panels

width.description: The column's share of its tier's width, relative to the other columns.
width.title: Width

Column.title: Column

Corner.description: Which corner of its parent an inset sits in.
Corner.title: Corner

Direction.description: Which way a comic is read: its progression, not the direction of its text.
Direction.title: Direction

Facing.description: Which way an actor is turned.
Facing.title: Facing

Fit.description: How a supplied picture fills the panel, keeping its own proportions.
Fit.title: Fit

anyOf.description: One font file, relative to the document, lettering every face: `fonts/Comic.ttf` stands for `{regular: fonts/Comic.ttf}`.

bold_italic.description: The font file a stressed word, `_word_`, is lettered in. Left out, it is `italic`, or `regular` when there is no italic, and a note says so.
bold_italic.title: Bold Italic

display.description: The font file sound effects are lettered in. Left out, the shipped display face, Bangers, whatever the other faces are.
display.title: Display

italic.description: The font file every caption but a `spoken` one is lettered in. Left out, they are set in `regular`.
italic.title: Italic

regular.description: The font file dialogue and `spoken` captions are lettered in, relative to the document. Written alone, as `font: fonts/Comic.ttf`, it letters every face.
regular.title: Regular

FontSpec.description: The font files a panel is lettered in, each a path relative to the document.
FontSpec.title: FontSpec

Horizon.description: Where the ground meets whatever is behind it.
Horizon.title: Horizon

Inset.description: A small panel set into a corner of another, and drawn over it.

at.description: The corner of its parent the inset sits in, a gutter in from both edges.

read.description: When the inset is read: `after` its parent, or `before` it.

size.description: The inset's width and height, as a fraction of its parent's: above 0, at most 0.5.
size.title: Size

use.description: The name of a panel under `panels:`, set into this one.
use.title: Use

Inset.title: Inset

InsetOrder.description: Whether an inset is read before the panel it sits in, or after it.
InsetOrder.title: InsetOrder

font.description: The font files to letter in, relative to the document: one file for every face, or one for each. Left out, Source Sans Pro.

size.description: The dialogue type size, in panel units; captions keep 30 parts in 35 of it. Left out, 3.5% of the height the panel letters against: its own, or one tier of a three-tier page.
size.title: Size

Mark.description: Something drawn around a character, rather than on them, to say how they are.
Mark.title: Mark

Mass.description: One tonal mass in the backdrop: what it is, how far back, how wide.

kind.description: What the mass is made of, which decides its silhouette: seven outdoor kinds of stuff and five indoor.

plane.description: How far back the mass sits, which decides its value and its draw order. A `foreground` mass is drawn over the cast.

spans.description: How much of the panel's width the mass covers: all of it, or its `left`, `center` or `right` part.

Mass.title: Mass

MassKind.description: What a tonal mass in the backdrop is made of.
MassKind.title: MassKind

PageFormat.description: The page every panel on it is laid out on.

bleed.description: How far the printed sheet runs past the trim on every side, so art that reaches the edge can be cut cleanly: 30 is 3 mm. Paper around the page; nothing on it moves.
bleed.title: Bleed

gutter.description: The gap between two panels, or two columns, side by side in a tier.
gutter.title: Gutter

margin.description: The blank border inside the page's edge, on all four sides.
margin.title: Margin

size.description: The page's width and height: the trim, the size the printed page is cut to, in the units a panel uses. Printed, a unit is a tenth of a millimetre.
size.title: Size

tier_gutter.description: The gap between two tiers, and between two panels stacked in a column. Wider than `gutter`, as in print, so a tier reads as one row.
tier_gutter.title: Tier Gutter

PageFormat.title: PageFormat

PageSpec.description: One page: tiers, top to bottom.

tiers.description: The page's tiers, top to bottom.
tiers.title: Tiers

PageSpec.title: PageSpec

Palette.description: What a panel is drawn in: the value ladder in grey, or its twin in colour.
Palette.title: Palette

anyOf.description: A panel's name, which stands for `{use: name}`.

bleed.description: Run the frame past the trim to the bleed line, with no border there: `true` on every side that reaches the page's margin, or a list of those sides.
bleed.title: Bleed

insets.description: Panels set into its corners, and drawn over it.
insets.title: Insets

use.description: The name of a panel under `panels:`. Writing the name alone means `{use: name}`.
use.title: Use

width.description: The panel's share of its tier's width, relative to its neighbours.
width.title: Width

margin.description: An inset on all four sides, in panel units. Balloons, captions and sound effects keep inside it; figures may run past it, as comics let them.
margin.title: Margin

size.description: The panel's width and height, `[width, height]`, in panel units: everything else is measured against them. Printed, a unit is a tenth of a millimetre.
size.title: Size

PartialPanelSpec.description:

PartialSettingSpec.description:
Where and when the panel happens: tonal masses, or a picture drawn elsewhere.

In a scene any of these may be inherited, so none is required here.

fit.description: How the picture fills the panel: `cover` fills it and crops what overhangs, equally on both sides; `contain` shows the whole picture. Left out, `cover`.

horizon.description: Where the ground meets what is behind it, which every mass is composed against: `high` shows more ground, `low` less.

image.description: A picture drawn elsewhere, behind the cast: a PNG or JPEG file, relative to the document. Only its size is read. Written instead of `place` and `masses`.
image.title: Image

masses.description: The backdrop as tonal masses, back to front: what a `place` expands into, written out. Write this, `place` or `image`, never two of them.
masses.title: Masses

place.description: A named place, which stands for the list of masses it expands into. Write this, `masses` or `image`, never two of them.

time.description: When the panel happens, which sets the two ends of the value ladder: the foreground's value and the atmosphere's.

weather.description: What the air is doing: `fog` veils the backdrop; `rain` and `snow` veil it as cloud, and fall over everything, the cast included.

PartialSettingSpec.title: SettingSpec

Place.description: A named setting, expanded into masses by the frontend.
Place.title: Place

PlacementZone.description: Where in the panel a balloon would prefer to sit.
PlacementZone.title: PlacementZone

Plane.description: How far back a mass sits, which decides both its draw order and its value.
Plane.title: Plane

Predicate.description: How one actor stands in relation to another.
Predicate.title: Predicate

anyOf.description: A staging sentence, `subject predicate object` -- for example `alice left_of bob`. Predicates: left_of, right_of, in_front_of, behind, looking_at, ground_shared_with.
anyOf.patternErrorMessage: Write 'subject predicate object', where the predicate is one of: left_of, right_of, in_front_of, behind, looking_at, ground_shared_with

object.description: The other actor id. For `looking_at`, it may be somebody heard from off panel.
object.title: Object

predicate.description: How the subject stands to the object: `left_of`, `right_of`, `in_front_of`, `behind`, `looking_at` or `ground_shared_with`.

subject.description: The actor id the relation is about.
subject.title: Subject

Relation.description: One staging fact, written as a sentence.
Relation.title: Relation

by.description: Who speaks: an actor id in the cast, whose mouth the tail points at. With `off_panel`, the name of somebody nobody draws.
by.title: By

kind.description: The balloon the line is carried in: `speech`, `thought`, `whisper` or `shout`.

off_panel.description: The speaker is outside the panel: `true`, or the side of the frame they are on. The tail ends on the frame there.
off_panel.title: Off Panel

prefer.description: Where the balloon would like to sit, one of nine zones of the panel. The weakest placement term: face avoidance and reading order override it.

size.description: `small` for a line muttered, said under the breath or weakly: smaller type, in a balloon that keeps its room.

text.description: The line, as one string; the compiler breaks it into lines. A word between underscores, `_word_`, is stressed, and lettered in bold italic.
text.title: Text

image.description: A picture drawn elsewhere, behind the cast: a PNG or JPEG file, relative to the document. Only its size is read. Written instead of `place` and `masses`.

SfxEvent.description: A sound effect: letters that are part of the picture.

arc.description: How far the line of letters bends, in degrees, from -120 to 120: positive bows its middle up, negative down.
arc.title: Arc

from.description: Written `from`: the actor id the sound comes from, which it is placed near.
from.title: From

hollow.description: `true` letters the effect as an outline with no fill, so the art shows through: an open effect.
hollow.title: Hollow

prefer.description: Where the effect would like to sit, one of nine zones of the panel: on its own, or as a pull on an effect that has a `from`.

rotate.description: How far the effect is turned clockwise, in degrees, from -45 to 45.
rotate.title: Rotate

size.description: How loud: `small`, `medium` or `large`, lettered at 1.6, 2.6 or 4 times the dialogue type size.

text.description: The sound, lettered exactly as written, in the display face.
text.title: Text

SfxEvent.title: SfxEvent

SfxSize.description: How big a sound effect is lettered, as a multiple of the dialogue type size.

ShotType.description: How tightly the camera frames the cast.

Side.description: A side of the panel's frame: where an off-panel speaker is, or where it bleeds.

Spans.description: How much of the panel's width a mass covers.

anyOf.description: A panel's name, which stands for `{use: name}`.

bleed.description: Run the frame past the trim to the bleed line, with no border there: `true` on every side that reaches the page's margin, or a list of those sides.

height.description: The panel's share of its column's height, relative to the others in it.

insets.description: Panels set into its corners, and drawn over it.

use.description: The name of a panel under `panels:`. Writing the name alone means `{use: name}`.

Tier.description: A row of panels read in turn, or of columns each read top to bottom.

columns.description: In place of `panels`: columns side by side, each a stack of panels read top to bottom before the next.
columns.title: Columns

height.description: The tier's share of the page's height, relative to the other tiers.
height.title: Height

panels.description: The panels in the tier, in reading order: left to right, or right to left for a comic read that way.
panels.title: Panels

slant.description: How far the gutters between the tier's panels lean, in degrees, from -30 to 30. Positive leans the top of each gutter to the right.
slant.title: Slant

Tier.title: Tier

TimeOfDay.description: When the panel happens, which shifts the whole value ladder.

TypeSize.description: How large a line of dialogue is lettered, against the panel's dialogue size.

Weather.description: What the air is doing between the reader and the panel.

camera.description: How the cast is framed: the shot, and the camera's height.

anyOf.description: Leaves a cast member this panel would inherit out of it, and every staging relation that names them.

cast.description: Who is in the panel: each actor id, chosen by the author, and the puppet that plays them or the figure a picture draws. Their order means nothing.
cast.title: Cast

direction.description: Which way the comic is read: `ltr` from the top left, `rtl` from the top right, as manga are -- panels, pages and the balloons in a panel. Its progression, not its text: the words in a balloon still read left to right. Written once for the whole document; the scene is never mirrored.

lettering.description: How the lettering is set: the dialogue type size, and the font files.

page.description: The format every page shares: its size, margin, gutters and bleed.

pages.description: The pages, in order, each a list of tiers top to bottom.
pages.title: Pages

palette.description: What the panel is drawn in: `mono`, the value ladder in grey, or `tinted`, each value in a colour with the same lightness. Colour never changes a value, so a tinted panel is, in monochrome, the mono one. Inherited like any default; a panel may have its own.

panel.description: The panel's frame: its size and margin, in panel units.

additionalProperties.description: A complete, validated panel: the language's real definition.

lettering.description: How the lettering is set: the dialogue type size, and the font files.

over.description: Name of a panel to inherit from. Only the differences need stating: mappings merge recursively and lists replace.

palette.description: What the panel is drawn in: `mono`, the value ladder in grey, or `tinted`, each value in a colour with the same lightness. Colour never changes a value, so a tinted panel is, in monochrome, the mono one. Inherited like any default; a panel may have its own.

panel.description: The panel's frame: its size and margin, in panel units.

say.description: A line of dialogue, in a balloon whose tail points at the speaker.

caption.description: A caption: a box in which the panel speaks in its own voice, with no tail.

sfx.description: A sound effect: letters lettered into the picture, with no balloon.

script.description: What is said and heard, in the order it is read: `say` for a balloon, `caption` for a box, `sfx` for a sound effect.

setting.description: Where and when the panel happens: a named place, tonal masses or a picture behind the cast, with the time of day and the weather.
